description: We are a team of B.Tech Engineering students. Our skills cover full-stack web development (MERN), backend and system design, AI and computer vision. Our team has has built many full-stack and AI projects. We are interested in scalable, backend-heavy systems and in turning complex data into tools people can use. The Lunar Landing Site Navigator fits that: we took expert-only ephemeris and terrain data and made it clear and fast for planners, educators and the public.
summary:
LUMEN (Lunar Horizon Mission Operations Navigator) is an interactive, high-fidelity lunar landing site evaluation and environmental simulation system. Designed for the Artemis era, LUMEN addresses the critical challenge of navigating the Moon's extreme South Pole—where the Sun skims the horizon at 1°–3°, casting elongated, rapidly shifting shadows across hazardous crater rims, while direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication is constrained by lunar topography.

By combining high-resolution *NASA LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter)* Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) with *JPL SPICE (DE440)* ephemeris, LUMEN computes continuous, 360-degree skyline horizons, real-time solar elevation, terrain masking, and line-of-sight link availability for any lunar coordinate or historic landing site (including Artemis III candidate zones and Chandrayaan-3). LUMEN equips mission planners, payload operators, and the scientific community with an autonomous, physics-grounded decision cockpit to verify landing site safety, maximize solar array exposure, and prevent catastrophic lunar night power depletion.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

LUMEN models the true physical environment of any location on the lunar surface through four synchronized modules:

1. 360° Real Terrain Horizon Viewport: Computes a continuous radial skyline profile using sub-pixel ray-marching against LOLA DEM elevation matrices (up to 20 m/pixel resolution). It displays real topography, cliffs, and ridges with true solar azimuth, apparent solar disk altitude, and Earth line-of-sight elevation.

2. Interactive 3D Moon & Heliocentric Orbit Visualizer:Features a 3D Moon globe with LROC surface basemaps synced with a celestial orbital simulator showing Earth-Moon orbital inclination ($5.14^\circ$), sub-solar points, DTE comms beams, and trajectory corridors.

3. Environmental Telemetry & Verification Matrix: Computes dynamic countdowns for consecutive daylight, impending crater rim shadow threats, and communication windows over 14-day lunar cycles.

4. LUMEN AI Mission Copilot: An intelligent assistant grounded in SPICE ephemeris and LOLA data that autonomously synthesizes payload descent scenarios, power contingency schedules, and scientific mission briefs exportable to PDF.

What benefits does it have?

* Mission De-risking: Prevents premature lander thermal or battery failure by identifying micro-shadowing from nearby crater ridges that traditional coarse topographic maps miss.

* Autonomous Payload Sequencing: Generates flight planning windows that maximize combined solar generation and Earth line-of-sight.

* Zero-Setup Accessibility: Browser-based, lightweight execution eliminates the need to install complex local GIS or command-line SPICE environments.

What is the intended impact of the project?

LUMEN accelerates lunar exploration planning for space agencies (NASA, ESA, ISRO), commercial CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) contractors, and university researchers. It democratizes mission architecture, turning raw, multi-gigabyte orbital laser altimetry and celestial kernels into immediate, actionable operational telemetry.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used:

* Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js / React Three Fiber, HTML5 Canvas, Leaflet.js, Vite.

* Backend & Scientific Core: Python 3.11, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy (radial horizon horizon profiling algorithm), SpiceyPy / CSPICE (NAIF SPICE toolkit), Uvicorn.

* Data Pipelines & Cartography: USGS Astrogeology WMS Services, NASA PDS Geosciences Node.

How is your project creative?

LUMEN bridges the gap between raw aerospace telemetry tables and human visual intuition. Instead of viewing abstract slope heatmaps, mission directors can "stand" at the landing coordinates and observe the Sun cresting or dipping behind the exact crater rim that their solar panels will face, creating a lunar mission control console in the browser.

What factors did your team consider?

* Lunar Libration & Ephemeris Fidelity: SPICE DE440 ephemeris accounts for lunar precession and nutation over multi-week mission timelines.

* Coordinate Inversion & Orientation: Rigorous adherence to selenographic coordinates (IAU Moon frame) and topocentric horizon azimuths.

* Accessibility & UI Ergonomics: High-contrast aerospace UI design, tabular numeric telemetry typography (JetBrains Mono) to eliminate visual jitter during real-time timeline scrubbing, and sub-second calculation caching.
